key_gap: Both sides reached the same verdict — reject the 90-day mandate — with identical base-rate math: P(success|fast) = 8/30 ≈ 27% vs P(success|slow) = 4/10 = 40% vs the 30% portfolio base rate, the '12/12 winners fast' headline falsified by the ledger (4 slow winners incl. the 7.2x largest exit), and the hidden cohort named (22/30 fast-launchers = 73% failed). The gap is ordering and ownership: the human opened with the failure-side question as the first move — 'where are the failures this pattern hides?' — and the denominator was in place before any policy talk, landing the overturn in one pass ('the 90-day rule is a base rate wearing a success story'); the AI re-derived population-conditioning inside its WHY stage before applying it, reaching the identical conclusion with scaffolding overhead and stating the insight later and more cautiously.
learning_signal: When a success-pattern claim arrives with a closed dataset, the failure-side question is the entire answer and must be the first move: (1) before evaluating any survivor pattern, demand the full denominator — every case, winners and losers — and rebuild the contingency table (feature x outcome over the whole population); (2) falsify the claim's headline against the records (a survivor-pattern claim that mis-states even one documented exception is already overturned); (3) compute the conditional rates against the base rate and read them as refuting the causal claim when the feature's cohort does not beat the population rate — a feature present in 75% of the population will be present in nearly all winners without meaning anything; (4) surface the hidden cohort explicitly (73% of the feature cohort failed) — that number is the overturning datum; (5) then and only then decide (here: reject the mandate, commission the discriminative analysis, name the n = 40 / no-confounder bound).
suggested_improvement: Add a 'denominator-first' gate to WHAT/WHY for empirical pattern claims: (a) if the brief asserts a survivor pattern (e.g., 'all our winners did X'), require the complete population table (feature x outcome) to be reconstructed BEFORE generating alternatives — treat a missing failure cohort as the first thing to look for, not a detail; (b) check the claim's factual headline against the records and falsify it explicitly when contradicted; (c) compute conditional rates vs the base rate and state whether the pattern beats the population rate (if not, the pattern is a prevalence artifact); (d) always emit the hidden cohort's failure count as a headline number; (e) only after this pass, decide — and if the data refutes the claim, reject the proposed policy, not just hedge it.

key_gap: The pure style executed its core move correctly and then failed on it: it asked for the failures, correctly inventoried that the counterfactual is structurally unobtainable (no untreated cohort, no reference class for a first-ever release, pre-hospital deaths unobservable in-window, no placebo arm possible), and then converted that correct diagnosis into a blocking demand — 'we cannot attest efficacy; withhold ratification until the evidence exists' — stalling expansion to 2,000-6,000 still-exposed people. The AI bounded the evidence instead: complete treated cohort (P(death|T) ≈ 1.4%, both deaths > 8h to care + severe cardiac disease vs all survivors ≤ 6h — an internal time-to-care gradient), mechanism plausibility, decision-appropriate evidence bar (not research-grade), and the decisive move: manufacture the missing data prospectively — standing registry, autopsy series, post-hoc case-control — so the counterfactual gets built going forward rather than blocking the decision now.
learning_signal: When failure data cannot exist, the demand for it is a failure mode, not rigor. Separating the evidence bar from the decision bar is the core skill: (1) inventory the failure side completely and state explicitly what is missing by structure (no control, no reference class, unobservable cohort) — do this honestly, then move on; (2) check value-of-information before demanding evidence: if the comparator cannot be built in the decision window or at all, the demand is a stall, not a standard; (3) weight what IS available — complete-cohort accounting, internal gradients (both deaths late-to-care + comorbidity vs all survivors within the window), mechanism plausibility — and decide on it; (4) when the counterfactual is unobtainable in retrospect, create it prospectively: registry, autopsy, post-hoc case-control — the missing data is manufactured forward, and that is part of the decision, not an objection to it; (5) name what is never measurable so the decision's bound is explicit, not silent.
suggested_improvement: Add a 'counterfactual impossibility check' to the WHY stage for emergency/novel-domain decisions: (a) after modeling, explicitly test whether the missing data (control arm, reference class, hidden cohort) could exist within the decision horizon — if not, classify the demand as impossible and lower the evidence bar to decision-appropriate; (b) run the gradient: search the available data for internal variation (time-to-treatment, severity, comorbidity) that discriminates outcomes within the complete cohort and use it as the primary evidence; (c) include a 'manufacture missing data forward' step in HOW — if the counterfactual cannot exist retrospectively, the selected plan must create it prospectively (registry/autopsy/case-control) as a mandatory component; (d) add a stall-cost line to the options table — quantify what withholding costs (exposure-hours without intervention) so 'refuse to decide on imperfect evidence' is priced like any other alternative.
